cluster_name: UK suspends Chagos Islands payments after Trump calls deal terrible
event_summary: UK PM Andy Burnham met US President Trump in New York on 22 September 2026; Trump called the UK-Mauritius Chagos Islands deal 'terrible'. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed annual payments to Mauritius of at least £120m are on hold pending a review.
tldr: Across 14 outlets in 10 countries, the near-unanimous bottom line is that the UK-Mauritius Chagos Islands agreement is effectively suspended because Washington said no — a convergence so complete it leaves UK agency largely invisible. US outlets focus on Trump's personal endorsement of Burnham over Starmer, treating the Chagos rebuke as incidental to a broader relationship reset; UK outlets focus on the financial and legal exposure — £120m a year on hold, a signed treaty in jeopardy. Asian and Southeast Asian outlets treat the suspension through the lens of Diego Garcia's strategic function, with US veto power read as the default logic of Indo-Pacific security. Mauritius — the counterparty to the deal and the African Union's preferred claimant to Chagos sovereignty — contributes no voice to this cluster, making the decolonisation dimension of the agreement invisible across the entire 10-country spread.

evidence.quote: Agreement with Mauritius must be revised to secure US backing and long-term future of Diego Garcia base, says British defense secretary
U.S. president lambasted deal over Diego Garcia military base.
Defence secretary places annual payments to Mauritius on hold as UK government reviews deal over Diego Garcia base
Donald Trump says he can do business with Andy Burnham at their first face-to-face meeting in New York, but criticises the "terrible" Chagos deal.
President Trump hailed the UK as a country bursting with potential that could be realised if only it had good leadership.
"No, I think they're up -- well, they're more up now than they were with your last prime minister, let me put it that way," Trump told reporters, referring to Keir Starmer.
UK will review its Chagos Islands deal with Mauritius after Trump criticised the agreement, with the future of the Diego Garcia base at the centre.
The deal would have given Britain a 99-year lease of the base, with the option to extend.
Trump praises new British PM Burnham but criticizes Chagos Islands agreement
Wes Streeting has said annual payments worth at least £120m to Mauritius are on hold as the government reconsiders its deal over the Chagos Islands, after Donald Trump refused to back the agreement.

frames.sub_frame: deal review to secure US backing

evidence.quote: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has confirmed the review after Donald Trump told Andy Burnham the deal was "terrible".
Tories say deal should be fully scrapped after it was criticised by Donald Trump during his meeting with Andy Burnham

silences.what_they_covered_instead: No Australian item in this cluster despite Australia's role in US-led Indo-Pacific security architecture and interest in Diego Garcia; Australian press appears to have prioritised domestic politics or Pacific affairs over the UK-Mauritius sovereignty dimension.

France backed Mauritius's Chagos sovereignty claim in UN votes and would normally carry Anglo-American diplomatic stories; absence suggests French-language press covered EU or domestic news rather than this UK-US bilateral angle.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Uniquely re-frames the meeting as Trump delivering a leadership critique of the UK at large — the 'good leadership' line implies the Chagos problem is a symptom of Labour governance rather than a discrete policy disagreement with Washington.
Leads with Trump's comparative endorsement of Burnham over Starmer as the primary story; the only outlet treating the relationship upgrade as the headline rather than the deal suspension.
Only outlet to frame the meeting as a 'diplomatic test' and note Burnham is Britain's sixth prime minister in a decade, contextualising the encounter against sustained UK political instability.
Sole outlet to report the specific £120m annual payment figure and that the payments are on hold; provides the only financial quantification of what the deal's suspension costs.

Makes explicit what others only imply: the deal must be revised to 'secure US backing' — foregrounding the conditionality and UK dependency rather than framing the review as a sovereign British choice.

Only outlet noting Trump brushed aside differences over the Middle East at the meeting, signalling the Chagos deal was not the only friction point and the bilateral agenda extended beyond the island dispute.

bottom_line: Trump's public rejection of the Chagos Islands deal at his first meeting with Burnham has effectively suspended a signed UK-Mauritius agreement and frozen £120m in annual payments. Across 14 outlets and 10 countries, coverage converges on the same conclusion — the deal cannot proceed without US approval — while Mauritius's perspective and the decolonisation dimension of the agreement go entirely unreported.
